FOREWORD This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards on 21 September 1989, after the draft finalized by the Sewing Machines Sectional Committee, had been approved by the Light Mechanical Engineering Division Council. In the series of standards on sewing machine components, this standard covers the flywheels. Three types of flywheels, namely spoked type, disc type and square type, commonly used for household sewing machines in the country, have been incorporated in this standard.

1 SCOPE 1.1 This standard lays down the requirements for three types of flywheels for sewing machines for household purposes. 2 REFERENCES Specification for grey iron casting ( third revision ) Electroplated coating of 1068 :1985 nickel plus chromium and copper plus nickel plus chromium on iron and steel General tolerances for 2102 ( P a r t 1) : 1980 dimensions and form and position : Part 1 General tolerances for linear and angular dimensions (second revision ) Sampling inspection table: 2500 ( P a r t 1) : 1973 Part 1 Inspection by attributes and by count of defects ( first revision ) Methods for randomsampl4905 : 1968 ing

3 NOMENCLATURE 3.1 Shall be as indicated in Fig. 1. 4 MATERIAL 4.1 The flywheel shall be made from cast iron conforming to grade FG 150 of IS 210 : 1978. 5 DIMENSIONS 5.1 The main dimension for flywheels shall be as given in Fig. 2, 3 and 4. 6 TOLERANCES 6.1 Tolerances shall be as indicated in Fig. 2, 3 and 4. 6.2 The tolerances on untoleranced dimensions shall be in accordance with medium class of IS 2102 ( Part 1 ) : 1980. 6.3 The minimum mass of the flywheels shall be as under: a) Spoked-type 750 g, b) Disc-type 725 g, and c) Square type 650 g.

A-1 SCALE OF SAMPLING A-1.3 If the flywheels are packed individually, in order to ensure the randomness of selection, IS 4905 : 1968 shall be used. A-1.4 If flywheels are packed in different cartons, a suitable number of cartons (not less than 20 percent of the total in the lot subject to a minimum of 2 ) shall be chosen at random. From each of the cartons, so chosen, an approximately equal number of flywheels shall be picked up from its different parts so as to obtain the required number of flywheels specified in col 2 of Table 1.

Standard Mark The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The Standard Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well defined system of inspection, testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by BIS and operated by the producer. Standard marked products are also continuously checked by BIS for conformity to that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the use of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards.

Bureau of Indian Standards BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 to promote harmonious development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods and attending to connected matters in the country. This does not preclude the free use, in the course of implementing the standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or grade designations. Enquiries relating to copyright be adressed to the Director ( Publications ), BIS. Users of Indian Standards should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition.
